ant_001: You can recognise it by its huge trunk, nearly five metres round, and wide canopy spreading 32 metres. It stands in the small square between the rectory and Sint-Willibrorduskerk.
ant_002: You can recognise it by its broad, high crown visible across the meadow. It stands opposite the entrance to the Sterckshof manor house, in Rivierenhof park.
ant_003: You can recognise it by its thick trunk, 4.10 metres round, the widest black locust recorded in Belgium. It stands in Hertoghepark, hemmed in by Desguinlei, Karel Oomsstraat and Markgravelei.
ant_006: You can recognise it by its 35 metre height and trunk running clear of branches for six metres before the crown begins. It stands beside the bridge on Eric Sasselaan.
ant_007: You can recognise it by the bronze plaque set into four chained posts around its base. It stands in the middle of the Grote Markt.
ant_008: You can recognise them as the collection of solitary trees and tree groups around the pond and open lawn. They stand in the park behind Kasteel Den Brandt.
